en: Heating liquid water to 100 degrees Celsius gives its molecules enough energy to escape into the air as water vapor.
When iron is exposed to oxygen and moisture, the atoms react to form a new, brittle chemical compound called rust.
Stirring sugar in warm water breaks the solid crystals into individual molecules that spread evenly throughout the liquid.
When liquid water freezes into ice, its molecules arrange into a rigid crystal structure that takes up more space.
Baking powder releases carbon dioxide gas when heated, causing pancake batter to expand and become light and fluffy.
Metals conduct heat quickly because their free electrons transfer thermal energy rapidly from the hot end to the cold end.
Solid dry ice absorbs heat from its surroundings and changes directly into carbon dioxide gas without becoming a liquid first.
Pouring a sand and water mixture through filter paper traps the solid sand while allowing the liquid water to pass through.
Stomach acid breaks down solid food by chemically reacting with it to change complex molecules into simpler, absorbable nutrients.
A magnet generates an invisible magnetic field that pulls the iron atoms inside a steel paperclip toward it.
A solid steel ship floats because its hollow hull displaces a volume of water that weighs more than the ship.
Cooling a saturated saltwater solution lowers the water's capacity to hold dissolved salt, causing the excess salt to form solid crystals.
